Folder names, and what OneOS checks first

Root deletes only an old copy OneOS kept (a folder named oneos.old-<time>), and not while it\'s in use: something is still open in it, a session in it is still running or never came back, or it\'s still linked to One UI\'s folders. A restart ends that.
When you switch, how it went shows here.
It was a test: %1$s was set up and checked but not started.
The session has ended. Collect the logs below to see how it went; your next switch replaces them.
The phone hasn\'t restarted since. If the switch didn\'t start, the logs say why.
Takes a minute or two. Nothing on the phone changes.

Numbers, Wi-Fi names and accounts were removed.
Look at them, or send them to the OneOS team

The switch and return logs, the other system\'s start-up logs and text reports on the phone\'s state. Lines about messages, contacts, Wi-Fi and places are dropped; numbers, IDs, emails, Wi-Fi names, accounts and file names are removed as they\'re read. Never screenshots or recordings.
OneOS only reads. Saved Wi-Fi names are read only to remove them from the logs; they\'re never saved or shared. Personal info is removed before anything is written.
The last session didn\'t return normally. This puts back the settings One UI had before it.
Only needed after a force restart during the session. If it returned normally, nothing changes.
OneOS puts back the settings One UI had when the session started, such as its language, from the copy it saved then. Only that session\'s own copy is used.
Try again, or send the logs to the OneOS team. The reason is under Details.
Clears this summary here and on Home until your next switch. The logs stay on the phone.

It holds an older system\'s apps and data, which %1$s can\'t use. They\'re kept as an old copy and %1$s starts fresh.
Needs about %1$s free. You confirm first.
Stops after the current file. The system is then not set up, and the switch stays off until you set it up again.
%1$s isn\'t needed now. If you set up again later, you\'ll need to download it once more.
Delete %1$s? The system set up from it stays.
It takes about 15 minutes; keep OneOS open and the phone plugged in. OneOS writes only in its own folder and checks every file before it\'s used.
Uses the file you downloaded for %1$s.
Reuses %1$s already on this phone; it\'s checked first (about a minute).

As root, through its root script, in /data/local/tmp/oneos only: the system image, the OneOS files, the installd table and the session settings. Root checks each file\'s size and SHA-256 before it is used. A folder OneOS 0.3.6 or earlier made under its old name is renamed first; nothing in it changes.
Every check, the folder as root read it, each step
As root, OneOS unpacks the image into /data/local/tmp/oneos (5 to 11 GB) and puts the OneOS files and session scripts next to it, checking each one\'s SHA-256. It takes about 15 minutes.

Setup writes only in OneOS\'s folder and deletes nothing outside it. What was set up before is kept as an old copy, and leftover files are moved to a folder inside OneOS\'s folder. One UI keeps running.
Hold Volume Up + Volume Down for 3 seconds
Works once %1$s is starting: One UI comes back, usually without a restart. While the OneOS logo still shows, use Force restart.
OneOS brings you back by itself
If %1$s doesn\'t finish starting, stops, or the screen stays black, One UI comes back by itself after a few minutes.
Hold Power + Volume Down until it restarts into One UI. Afterwards, tap Restore One UI\'s settings in Advanced.
If root needs turning on again after a restart, do that, then open OneOS. Last session shows how it went.
Every check again: root, the set-up system, the screen lock, battery and free space. Nothing on the phone changes.
One UI closes while %1$s is set up and checked, then One UI comes back. %1$s doesn\'t start.
Every check runs again, then One UI closes and %1$s starts

Experimental. Takes this phone\'s own Samsung calling service (IMS) into the other system so calls can use VoLTE instead of 3G. Nothing is sent to anyone; One UI\'s files are only read. May not work yet.

Experimental. One UI\'s camera service asks Knox on every camera open and waits 5 seconds for a service the other system does not have, so the camera app gives up first. This answers for it. If the camera stops working with this on, turn it back off.
Switch with a screen lock set

Normally OneOS will not switch while a PIN, pattern, password, fingerprint or face lock is on. Your One UI apps and photos are encrypted behind that lock: if a session leaves the phone unable to accept it, the only way back is a factory reset, which erases everything. This has happened to a tester. Turn this on only if you accept that risk.
Leaves Play services and the Play Store out of %1$s this time only. Nothing else changes.
Google apps are hidden this time.

One UI closes and %1$s starts in about a minute. %2$s

Apps you install in %1$s can reach One UI's data if they get root: install only ones you trust.

OneOS closes with One UI.
To come back, hold Volume Up + Volume Down for 3 seconds once it\'s starting. Stuck on the OneOS logo? Hold Power + Volume Down.
To come back, tap Back to One UI in %1$s, or hold Volume Up + Volume Down for 3 seconds. Stuck on the OneOS logo? Hold Power + Volume Down.
It switches the phone into another system without flashing. Things can break.
Remove your PIN, pattern, password, fingerprint and face unlock before switching. If the phone gets stuck restarting, a locked phone may not let you recover it.
Apps in the other system can get the same root as One UI. One that does could reach One UI\'s data: install only apps you trust, and never grant root to ones you don\'t know.
Tested on the Z Fold (F8U), S26 Ultra, S25 Ultra and S25.
Runs another Android system next to One UI on a rooted phone, and comes back to One UI, usually without a restart. Nothing is flashed.

Sets up a system you downloaded in its own folder and switches to it. Back to One UI or Volume Up + Down brings you back. OneOS downloads nothing itself and deletes nothing outside its folder without asking.
Tested on the Z Fold (F8U), S26 Ultra, S25 Ultra and S25. Other phones are untested.
Every change OneOS makes as root is checked first, by the app and by root. Nothing outside OneOS\'s folder is ever deleted, and the other system is kept away from One UI\'s data.
Setup and the switch run their own checks and stop anything this phone can\'t run.
Removes these logs from OneOS. The phone keeps its own copy in OneOS\'s folder until your next switch.
The app and the changes OneOS makes to each system. Its session scripts started from the project credited below.
